Question Choices: Two prisms have the same number of cubes. Prism A uses bigger cubes, prism B uses smaller cubes. Which one has larger volume?
Hints: Compare volume per cube when counts are equal.
Solution: Both prisms contain the same positive number of cubes. Each cube in A occupies more space, so count × cube volume is larger for A.

Question Choices: A prism has dimensions: length = 2/5, width = 5/6, height = 3/4. Find the volume
Hints: Convert mixed numbers first, then multiply and simplify.
Solution: Convert any mixed dimensions to improper fractions. Volume=length×width×height=(2/5)×(5/6)×(3/4)=1/4 cubic units. Multiplying numerators and denominators gives 30/120; divide both by 30 to obtain 1/4.

Question Choices: A prism has dimensions: length = 1 1/3, width = 3/8, height = 4/5. Find the volume
Hints: Convert mixed numbers first, then multiply and simplify.
Solution: Convert any mixed dimensions to improper fractions. Volume=length×width×height=(4/3)×(3/8)×(4/5)=2/5 cubic units. Multiplying numerators and denominators gives 48/120; divide both by 24 to obtain 2/5.

Question Choices: A prism has dimensions: length = 2 1/2, width = 2/5, height = 1 1/2. Find the volume. Simplify the fraction to a mixed number
Hints: Convert mixed numbers first, then multiply and simplify.
Solution: Convert any mixed dimensions to improper fractions. Volume=length×width×height=(5/2)×(2/5)×(3/2)=3/2 cubic units. As a mixed number, 3/2=1 1/2. Multiplying numerators and denominators gives 30/20; divide both by 10 to obtain 3/2.
